questions.stem: Which of the following structures is the largest artery in the human body?
questions.explanation: The aorta is the main systemic artery that originates from the left ventricle and supplies the entire body; it is larger than the pulmonary, carotid, and subclavian arteries.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is the most common site of a duodenal ulcer perforation?
options: A. Posterior wall of the first part of the duodenum
B. Anterior wall of the third part of the duodenum
C. Posterior wall of the third part of the duodenum
D. Anterior wall of the first part of the duodenum
questions.explanation: Duodenal ulcers most frequently occur on the posterior wall of the first part of the duodenum, making this the most common perforation site. The other options represent less common locations.
questions.source: Basic anatomy of the duodenum; common ulcer perforation sites

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man undergoes a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The surgeon identifies a cystic duct that drains into the common hepatic duct at a 45° angle. Which of the following structures is most likely to be injured if the cystic duct is inadvertently divided during the procedure?
questions.explanation: The cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct; dividing it will transect the common hepatic duct, leading to bile leakage. The cystic artery runs separately with the duct, the lymph node is not a vascular structure, and the gallbladder fundus is distal to the duct.
questions.source: Basic surgical anatomy of the hepatobiliary system

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a palpable mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑encapsulated lesion arising from the left hepatic lobe. Which of the following structures is most likely to be displaced by this tumour?
questions.explanation: A hepatic tumour in the left lobe typically displaces the left hepatic artery, which runs anterior to the portal vein and duct. The portal vein and duct lie more posteriorly, while the adrenal gland is located superiorly and posterior to the liver.
questions.source: Basic hepatic anatomy; relationship of vessels to liver lobes

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a 3‑month history of intermittent right upper quadrant pain and a palpable mass in the epigastrium. Imaging shows a cystic lesion arising from the posterior wall of the stomach, with a thick, irregular wall and a small, enhancing nodule on the inner surface. Which of the following structures is most likely to be involved in the malignant transformation of this lesion?
questions.explanation: The lesion described is a gastric cystic neoplasm with an enhancing nodule, characteristic of a cystic gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST). GISTs arise from the interstitial cells of Cajal located in the muscularis propria layer. Thus the muscularis propria is the structure most likely involved in malignant transformation. The mucosa, submucosa and serosa are not the origin of GISTs.
